knowledge:
- key_parameters: filePath=path to the tab-separated input file containing peptide-level measurements ;; group1=character vector of sample names for the first comparison group ;; group2=character vector of sample names for the second comparison group ;; normalize=character string (e.g., "true") indicating whether to normalize the AffyBatch object ;; affy=an AffyBatch object containing the probe-level microarray data
- alternatives: Standard workflows that pre-calculate gene/protein-level values before differential analysis (such as standard limma or genefilter on summarized expression sets)
- when_to_use: Use when you have probe-level Affymetrix microarray data or peptide-level proteomics data and want to compute differential expression using probe-level change averaging (PECA) to retain low-level statistical power
- pitfalls: Quality control and filtering of the data (e.g., based on low intensity or probe specificity) are not performed by PECA and must be done beforehand by the user ;; Column names in the input TSV must not start with a number or contain special characters ;; The first column of the TSV must contain the protein/gene ID for summarization

workflows.name: peca_proteomics_tsv
workflows.intent: Identify differential protein expression from peptide-level measurements in a TSV file.
input: peptides.tsv (tab-separated text file containing peptide-level intensity measurements with protein IDs in the first column and sample columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Define sample groups ;; 2. Run PECA on the TSV file using PECA_tsv
workflows.code:
library(PECA)
group1 <- c("A1", "A2", "A3")
group2 <- c("B1", "B2", "B3")
results <- PECA_tsv(filePath, group1, group2)

workflows.name: peca_microarray_affy
workflows.intent: Identify differential gene expression from Affymetrix microarray probe-level data.
input: SpikeIn133 (an AffyBatch object containing probe-level microarray data)
workflows.stages: 1. Subset or prepare the AffyBatch object ;; 2. Run PECA on the AffyBatch object using PECA_AffyBatch
